name: Media & framing
description: Community pack: headline framing, selective quotation, and media techniques.
author: Aletheia Community

patterns.name: Headline–body mismatch
patterns.description: The headline implies a stronger, more emotional, or different claim than the article body supports.
examples: Headline: 'Study proves X causes Y'. Body: small correlational study with many limitations.
counterMeasures: Read past the headline before updating beliefs.
Compare the title claim to the strongest claim the body actually makes.

patterns.name: Selective quotation
patterns.description: Quoting a fragment that reverses or exaggerates the speaker's intended meaning.
examples: Cutting 'I do not believe that...' so only the opposite-sounding clause remains.
counterMeasures: Seek the full paragraph or primary source.
Ask what was left out of the quote.

patterns.name: False balance
patterns.description: Presenting a fringe view as equally supported by evidence as a well-established one for the appearance of neutrality.
detectionHints: experts disagree framing without weight of evidence
both sides when one side lacks evidence
false equivalence of consensus and outlier
examples: Equal airtime to climate science and denial as if the evidence bases were comparable.
counterMeasures: Ask for the weight of evidence, not just presence of disagreement.
Check whether 'both sides' reflects reality or a narrative need.
